# Working with AI Agents

Coding agents are part of the team. Hold them to the same standards as everyone else, and write those standards down where the agent reads them.

---

## Instructions in the Repository

- Every repository has an agent instructions file (for example `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`) with the rules that matter there: how to branch, what not to touch, how to run the checks
- Personal or organisation defaults live in one shared file; the repository's own file wins where they differ
- When the same correction comes up in two projects, it belongs in the shared file, not in one agent's memory

---

## Outward Actions

Anything other people see (messages, issues, pull requests, merges, published pages) is drafted first, unless the owner has said to send it.

- No AI attribution in commits, pull requests or comments. The author is the person who owns the change
- Keep quiet hours: nothing outward overnight
- Pace actions that notify people: merges at least ten minutes apart with the main branch green, tracker status changes a minute apart, replies not seconds after a question
- Never delete or overwrite shared things (labels, tickets, branches, data) without saying what goes and keeping a record

---

## Decisions and Verification

- Decisions belong to their owner. The agent prepares the question and the options; it does not decide
- Check what is claimed. Run the build, query the data, read the file
- Say plainly what was not verified
- Measure rather than guess, and correct an estimate that turns out wrong

---

## Data and Secrets

- Agents follow [Security and compliance](../security/security-and-compliance.md): least personal data, no special-category data without a recorded decision
- Never put a secret, or a file of real records, into a prompt or a chat. Work with counts and checks instead
- An agent's conversation logs can hold whatever it read. Treat them as the most sensitive data the agent touched
